claim: CD4+ T cell activation is driven by five-module receptor complexes.
source: CD4+ T cell activation is driven by five-module receptor complexes.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract that establishes the multi-module nature of CD4+ T cell receptors.

claim: The T cell receptor (TCR) is the receptor module that binds composite surfaces of peptide antigens embedded within MHCII molecules (pMHCII).
source: The T cell receptor (TCR) is the receptor module that binds composite surfaces of peptide antigens embedded within MHCII molecules (pMHCII).
evidence: This describes the established function of TCR based on scientific consensus.

claim: TCR associates with three signaling modules (CD3γε, CD3δε, and CD3ζζ) to form TCR-CD3 complexes.
source: It associates with three signaling modules (CD3γε, CD3δε, and CD3ζζ) to form TCR-CD3 complexes.
evidence: This describes the known composition of the TCR-CD3 complex.

claim: CD4 reciprocally associates with TCR-CD3-pMHCII assemblies on the outside of a CD4+ T cells and with the Src kinase, LCK, on the inside.
source: It reciprocally associates with TCR-CD3-pMHCII assemblies on the outside of a CD4+ T cells and with the Src kinase, LCK, on the inside.
evidence: This describes the dual binding function of CD4 based on established knowledge.

claim: The CD4 transmembrane GGXXG and cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (C/F)CV+C motifs found in eutherian (placental mammal) CD4 have constituent residues that evolved under purifying selection.
source: Previously, we reported that the CD4 transmembrane GGXXG and cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (C/F)CV+C motifs found in eutherian (placental mammal) CD4 have constituent residues that evolved under purifying selection (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This cites prior work by the authors showing evolutionary conservation of these motifs.

claim: Expressing mutants of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together in T cell hybridomas increased CD4-LCK association.
source: Expressing mutants of these motifs together in T cell hybridomas increased CD4-LCK association but reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation levels, as well as IL-2 production, in response to agonist pMHCII.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Expressing mutants of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together in T cell hybridomas reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation levels in response to agonist pMHCII.
source: Expressing mutants of these motifs together in T cell hybridomas increased CD4-LCK association but reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation levels, as well as IL-2 production, in response to agonist pMHCII.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Expressing mutants of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together in T cell hybridomas reduced IL-2 production in response to agonist pMHCII.
source: Expressing mutants of these motifs together in T cell hybridomas increased CD4-LCK association but reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation levels, as well as IL-2 production, in response to agonist pMHCII.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motif mutants preferentially localized CD4-LCK pairs to non-raft membrane fractions.
source: Because these mutants preferentially localized CD4-LCK pairs to non-raft membrane fractions, one explanation for our results was that they impaired proximal signaling by sequestering LCK away from TCR-CD3.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Intracellular CD4-LCK interactions are not necessary for pMHCII-specific signal initiation.
source: Using T cell hybridomas, our results indicate that: intracellular CD4-LCK interactions are not necessary for pMHCII-specific signal initiation
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are key determinants of CD4-mediated pMHCII-specific signal amplification.
source: the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are key determinants of CD4-mediated pMHCII-specific signal amplification
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs exert their functions independently of direct CD4-LCK association.
source: the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs exert their functions independently of direct CD4-LCK association.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The data provide a mechanistic explanation for why residues within the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are under purifying selection in jawed vertebrates.
source: These data provide a mechanistic explanation for why residues within these motifs are under purifying selection in jawed vertebrates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings in evolutionary context.

claim: The design of conventional single-chain chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) was informed by an early 1990s understanding of receptor biology.
source: For example, the design of conventional single-chain chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) utilized in CAR-T cell therapy was informed by an early 1990s understanding of receptor biology and bears little resemblance to the multi-module receptors that naturally drive T cell responses.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical development of CAR design.

claim: Conventional CARs bear little resemblance to the multi-module receptors that naturally drive T cell responses.
source: the design of conventional single-chain chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) utilized in CAR-T cell therapy was informed by an early 1990s understanding of receptor biology and bears little resemblance to the multi-module receptors that naturally drive T cell responses.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about CAR structure versus natural receptors.

claim: Redirecting CD4+ T cells with CARs is important for long-lived therapeutic efficacy.
source: In particular, understanding how CD4+ T cells respond to antigen is important for informing biomimetic engineering of CARs because recent data show that redirecting CD4+ T cells with CARs is important for long-lived therapeutic efficacy (Melenhorst et al., 2022).
evidence: This cites recent findings about CAR-T cell therapy.

claim: Each naïve CD4+ T cell expresses a clonotypic receptor module, called the T cell receptor (TCR), that binds specifically to unique features of composite pMHCII surfaces.
source: Each naïve CD4+ T cell expresses a clonotypic receptor module, called the T cell receptor (TCR), that binds specifically to unique features of composite pMHCII surfaces (Kuhns and Badgandi, 2012; Kuhns and Davis, 2012).
evidence: This describes the clonotypic nature of TCR with citation support.

claim: The TCR lacks intracellular signaling domains.
source: The TCR lacks intracellular signaling domains and instead assembles with three signaling modules (CD3γε, δε, and ζζ) that have immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs), and other motifs, to connect TCR-pMHCII interactions to the intracellular signaling apparatus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TCR structure.

claim: CD3 signaling modules have immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs).
source: The TCR lacks intracellular signaling domains and instead assembles with three signaling modules (CD3γε, δε, and ζζ) that have immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs), and other motifs, to connect TCR-pMHCII interactions to the intracellular signaling apparatus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CD3 structure.

claim: CD4 binds pMHCII in a reciprocal fashion with TCR-CD3 on the outside of CD4+ T cells.
source: CD4 is the coreceptor module. It binds pMHCII in a reciprocal fashion with TCR-CD3 on the outside of CD4+ T cells and interacts with the Src kinase, LCK, via an intracellular CQC zinc clasp motif and helix (Huse et al., 1998; Kim et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes CD4 binding with citation support.

claim: CD4 interacts with LCK via an intracellular CQC zinc clasp motif and helix.
source: It binds pMHCII in a reciprocal fashion with TCR-CD3 on the outside of CD4+ T cells and interacts with the Src kinase, LCK, via an intracellular CQC zinc clasp motif and helix (Huse et al., 1998; Kim et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of CD4-LCK interaction with citation support.

claim: According to the TCR signaling paradigm, co-engagement of pMHCII by TCR-CD3 and CD4 positions LCK and the CD3 ITAMs in the proper spatial proximity to enable LCK phosphorylation of the CD3 ITAMs to initiate signaling.
source: According to the TCR signaling paradigm, co-engagement of pMHCII by TCR-CD3 and CD4 positions LCK and the CD3 ITAMs in the proper spatial proximity to enable LCK phosphorylation of the CD3 ITAMs to initiate signaling (Rudd, 2021).
evidence: This describes the prevailing model with citation.

claim: CD4-LCK interactions are not key determinants of CD3ζ ITAM phosphorylation.
source: However, when we tested this model directly we found that CD4-LCK interactions are not key determinants of CD3ζ ITAM phosphorylation (pCD3ζ) (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This reports findings from prior work that challenge the prevailing model.

claim: C-terminally truncated CD4 lacking the motifs that mediate CD4-LCK interactions can drive CD4+ T cell development, proliferation, and T-helper functions.
source: Based on our work and that of other labs, including a study showing that C-terminally truncated CD4 lacking the motifs that mediate CD4-LCK interactions can nevertheless drive CD4+ T cell development, proliferation, and T-helper functions, we consider the question of how intracellular pMHCII-specific CD4+ T cell signaling is initiated to be unresolved (Glassman et al., 2018; Horkova et al., 2023; Killeen and Littman, 1993; Xu and Littman, 1993).
evidence: This cites multiple studies showing truncated CD4 can function.

claim: The question of how intracellular pMHCII-specific CD4+ T cell signaling is initiated is unresolved.
source: we consider the question of how intracellular pMHCII-specific CD4+ T cell signaling is initiated to be unresolved (Glassman et al., 2018; Horkova et al., 2023; Killeen and Littman, 1993; Xu and Littman, 1993).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on cited evidence.

claim: Mutating the intracellular CQC clasp and IKRLL helix motifs resulted in significant reductions in CD4-LCK association.
source: When we mutated the intracellular CQC clasp and IKRLL helix motifs that are known to mediate CD4-LCK interactions, we observed significant reductions in CD4-LCK association; yet we did not observe the predicted decrease in CD3ζ ITAM phosphorylation (pCD3ζ).
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Mutating the intracellular CQC clasp and IKRLL helix motifs did not result in the predicted decrease in CD3ζ ITAM phosphorylation.
source: When we mutated the intracellular CQC clasp and IKRLL helix motifs that are known to mediate CD4-LCK interactions, we observed significant reductions in CD4-LCK association; yet we did not observe the predicted decrease in CD3ζ ITAM phosphorylation (pCD3ζ).
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work that contradict predictions.

claim: Mutating the transmembrane GGXXG motif and cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (C/F)CV+C palmitoylation motif increased the frequency of CD4-LCK pairs preferentially localized to detergent soluble membrane (DSM) domains.
source: In contrast, when we mutated the transmembrane GGXXG motif and cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (C/F)CV+C palmitoylation motif, we observed an increased frequency of CD4-LCK pairs that were preferentially localized to detergent soluble membrane (DSM) domains.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs resulted in reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation compared with WT CD4.
source: We also found evidence of reduced CD3ζ, ZAP70, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation (pCD3ζ, pZAP70, and pPLCγ1) compared with WT CD4.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from prior work.

claim: Truncating CD4 relieved CD4-LCK interactions.
source: As expected from prior work, truncating CD4 relieved CD4-LCK interactions and reduced IL-2 production.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study consistent with prior work.

claim: Truncating CD4 reduced IL-2 production.
source: As expected from prior work, truncating CD4 relieved CD4-LCK interactions and reduced IL-2 production.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: Truncating CD4 had no impact on the average pCD3ζ levels when compared with WT CD4, despite significantly reduced levels of CD4-LCK pairs.
source: However, there was no impact on the average pCD3ζ levels or the percent of cells with phosphorylated CD3ζ when compared with WT CD4, despite significantly reduced levels of CD4-LCK pairs.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: Truncating CD4 had no impact on the percent of cells with phosphorylated CD3ζ when compared with WT CD4.
source: However, there was no impact on the average pCD3ζ levels or the percent of cells with phosphorylated CD3ζ when compared with WT CD4, despite significantly reduced levels of CD4-LCK pairs.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: The core tenet of the TCR signaling paradigm, wherein CD4 recruits LCK to CD3 ITAMs to initiate signaling, needs revising.
source: These data provide further evidence that the core tenet of the TCR signaling paradigm, wherein CD4 recruits LCK to CD3 ITAMs initiates signaling, needs revising.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced IL-2 production.
source: Importantly, T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced IL-2 production as well as pCD3ζ levels and other TCR-proximal signaling events.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced pCD3ζ levels.
source: Importantly, T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced IL-2 production as well as pCD3ζ levels and other TCR-proximal signaling events.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced other TCR-proximal signaling events.
source: Importantly, T1 molecules bearing mutations in the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together reduced IL-2 production as well as pCD3ζ levels and other TCR-proximal signaling events.
evidence: This reports experimental findings from the current study.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs influence pMHCII-specific proximal signaling independently of CD4-LCK interactions.
source: The simplest interpretation of these data is that the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are key determinants of pMHCII-specific signaling on their own, independent of CD4-LCK interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree clusters mammalian CD4 sequences.
source: The maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree clusters mammalian CD4 sequences.
evidence: This describes Figure 1 showing phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Black dots in Figure 1 indicate dN/dS ratios that are significantly below 1 across the entire dataset.
source: Black dots indicate dN/dS ratios that are significantly below 1 across the entire dataset.
evidence: This describes the evolutionary analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Red dots in Figure 1 indicate residues under purifying selection in the mammalian only dataset.
source: Red dots indicate residues under purifying selection in the mammalian only dataset.
evidence: This describes the evolutionary analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: The T1 mutant produced measurable IL-2 at approximately 61% of WT response magnitude.
source: The T1 mutant produced measurable IL-2 (response magnitude ~61% of WT, Table 2) that was consistently reduced across a range of MCC peptide concentrations compared to WT
evidence: This reports experimental findings with quantitative data.

claim: The T1Δbind mutant did not produce IL-2.
source: whereas the T1Δbind mutant did not produce IL-2.
evidence: This reports experimental findings.

claim: Reduced pMHCII-specific endocytosis was observed for T1 and T1Δbind compared to WT.
source: We also observed reduced pMHCII-specific endocytosis for T1 and T1Δbind compared to WT (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: Extracellular CD4-pMHCII engagement is essential for IL-2 production in the experimental system.
source: These data indicate that, in our system, extracellular CD4-pMHCII engagement is essential for IL-2 production while the CD4 intracellular domain C-terminal of R422 contributes to IL-2 production, but is not absolutely necessary in the absence of other elements of the intracellular domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The CD4 intracellular domain C-terminal of R422 contributes to IL-2 production but is not absolutely necessary.
source: These data indicate that, in our system, extracellular CD4-pMHCII engagement is essential for IL-2 production while the CD4 intracellular domain C-terminal of R422 contributes to IL-2 production, but is not absolutely necessary in the absence of other elements of the intracellular domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The T1Δbind mutant significantly reduced pCD3ζ, pZAP70, and pPLCγ1 levels compared to the T1 control.
source: In comparison, the T1Δbind mutant significantly reduced pCD3ζ, pZAP70, or pPLCγ1 levels compared to the T1 control but, interestingly, did not impact the percent of cells responding to agonist MCC:I-Ek (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The T1Δbind mutant did not impact the percent of cells responding to agonist MCC:I-Ek.
source: In comparison, the T1Δbind mutant significantly reduced pCD3ζ, pZAP70, or pPLCγ1 levels compared to the T1 control but, interestingly, did not impact the percent of cells responding to agonist MCC:I-Ek (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: CD4 enhances the number of TCR-CD3 complexes per cell with phosphorylated CD3ζ molecules at Y142 in a manner dependent on TCR-CD3 and CD4 co-engagement of pMHCII but independent of the intracellular domain C-terminal of R422.
source: Because the antibodies used to detect pCD3ζ, pZAP70, and pPLCγ1 recognize single phosphorylated tyrosines, these data indicate that CD4 enhances the number of TCR-CD3 complexes per cell with phosphorylated CD3ζ molecules at Y142 (same in human and mouse), as well as the number of phosphorylated ZAP70 and PLCγ1 molecules per cell, in a manner that is dependent on TCR-CD3 and CD4 co-engagement of pMHCII but independent of the intracellular domain C-terminal of R422.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The average pCD3ζ levels for three independently generated T1Δbind mutants was 54.86% of the T1 control (p<0.001).
source: A key takeaway is that the average pCD3ζ levels for three independently generated T1Δbind mutants was 54.86% of the T1 control (p<0.001).
evidence: This reports quantitative experimental findings with statistical significance.

claim: CD3ζ phosphorylation occurs upon TCR engagement of cognate pMHCII in the absence of CD4-pMHCII interactions.
source: CD3ζ phosphorylation therefore occurs upon TCR engagement of cognate pMHCII in the absence of CD4-pMHCII interactions, and CD4 engagement of pMHCII increases the number of phosphorylated TCR-CD3 complexes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: CD4 engagement of pMHCII increases the number of phosphorylated TCR-CD3 complexes.
source: CD3ζ phosphorylation therefore occurs upon TCR engagement of cognate pMHCII in the absence of CD4-pMHCII interactions, and CD4 engagement of pMHCII increases the number of phosphorylated TCR-CD3 complexes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The pCD3ζ levels observed in the T1Δbind mutants is subthreshold for IL-2 production at the bulk population level.
source: Importantly, the pCD3ζ levels observed in the T1Δbind mutants is subthreshold for IL-2 production at the bulk population level.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: pMHCII-specific baseline pCD3ζ levels achieved in the absence of CD4-pMHCII interactions are approximately half of that achieved when CD4 can interact with pMHCII.
source: These results allow us to conclude that pMHCII-specific baseline pCD3ζ levels achieved in our system in the absence of CD4-pMHCII interactions are approximately half of that achieved when CD4 can interact with pMHCII on the outside of the cell.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: CD4-pMHCII interactions on the outside of the cell appear to be essential to push pCD3ζ levels above the threshold level needed for IL-2 production.
source: Furthermore, consistent with the kinetic discrimination model of T cell activation, CD4-pMHCII interactions on the outside of the cell appear to be essential to push pCD3ζ levels above the threshold level needed for IL-2 production (Rabinowitz et al., 1996).
evidence: This is an interpretation consistent with a cited model.

claim: Significantly reduced CD4-LCK association was observed in detergent resistant membranes (DRMs) for T1 compared to WT.
source: We observed significantly reduced CD4-LCK association in detergent resistant membranes (DRMs, aka membrane rafts) and DSMs for T1 compared to WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Pike, 2006).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: Significantly reduced CD4-LCK association was observed in DSMs for T1 compared to WT.
source: We observed significantly reduced CD4-LCK association in detergent resistant membranes (DRMs, aka membrane rafts) and DSMs for T1 compared to WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Pike, 2006).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motif mutants did not impact residual CD4-LCK association in the DRMs or DSMs.
source: The mutants did not impact residual CD4-LCK association in the DRMs or DSMs.
evidence: This reports experimental findings.

claim: The total LCK signal associated with CD4 was significantly lower for T1 compared with the WT.
source: Furthermore, the total LCK signal associated with CD4 was significantly lower for T1 compared with the WT, and the residual association was not impacted by the mutants (Table 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to table and figure.

claim: The residual CD4-LCK association in T1 was not impacted by the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motif mutants.
source: Furthermore, the total LCK signal associated with CD4 was significantly lower for T1 compared with the WT, and the residual association was not impacted by the mutants (Table 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to table and figure.

claim: The T1-TMD reduced the IL-2 response magnitude and sensitivity relative to the T1 control.
source: Here again, T1 was slightly lower than WT, while the T1-TMD reduced the IL-2 response magnitude and sensitivity relative to the T1 control (Figure 3A).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: Mutating the GGXXG or (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together did not impact pMHCII-induced TCR endocytosis relative to the T1 control.
source: Mutating the GGXXG or (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together did not impact pMHCII-induced TCR endocytosis relative to the T1 control, and activation-induced CD4 endocytosis was inhibited for all truncated CD4 molecules (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: Activation-induced CD4 endocytosis was inhibited for all truncated CD4 molecules.
source: Mutating the GGXXG or (C/F)CV+C motifs individually or together did not impact pMHCII-induced TCR endocytosis relative to the T1 control, and activation-induced CD4 endocytosis was inhibited for all truncated CD4 molecules (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: The T1-Palm(2C), T1-TP(2C), T1-Palm(3C), and T1-TP(3C) all reduced IL-2 production relative to T1.
source: The T1-Palm(2C), T1-TP(2C), T1-Palm(3C), and T1-TP(3C) all reduced IL-2 production relative to T1, indicating that they also influence the LCK-independent contribution of CD4 to pMHCII-specific signaling (Figure 3B).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: The T1-TP(2C) IL-2 response magnitude was lower than that of T1-Palm(2C) alone.
source: Of note, the T1-TP(2C) IL-2 response magnitude was lower than that of T1-Palm(2C) alone, consistent with what we previously observed with the full-length versions of these CD4 mutants (Figure 3B; Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure and prior work.

claim: The T1-Palm(3C) response magnitude was lower than that of T1-Palm(2C).
source: Furthermore, the T1-Palm(3C) response magnitude was lower than that of T1-Palm(2C), suggesting that the additional cysteine contributes to signaling.
evidence: This reports experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: The additional cysteine in the (C/F)CV+C motif contributes to signaling.
source: Furthermore, the T1-Palm(3C) response magnitude was lower than that of T1-Palm(2C), suggesting that the additional cysteine contributes to signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs contribute to the signaling cascade that leads to pMHCII-specific IL-2 production when CD4 does not directly interact with LCK.
source: Together, these data indicate that the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs contribute to the signaling cascade that leads to pMHCII-specific IL-2 production when CD4 does not directly interact with LCK via the intracellular CQC clasp and IKRLL motifs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The T1-TP(2C) cells made approximately half as much IL-2 as the T1 controls in response to APCs used in signaling studies.
source: We found that the T1-TP(2C) cells made approximately half as much IL-2 as the T1 controls, whereas IL-2 production by the T1Δbind cells was negligible (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: IL-2 production by the T1Δbind cells was negligible in response to APCs used in signaling studies.
source: We found that the T1-TP(2C) cells made approximately half as much IL-2 as the T1 controls, whereas IL-2 production by the T1Δbind cells was negligible (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figure.

claim: The ability of CD4 to interact with pMHCII can partially overcome the loss of function of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs at high ligand densities with respect to IL-2 production.
source: These data indicate that the ability of CD4 to interact with pMHCII can partially overcome the loss of function of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs at high ligand densities with respect to a downstream signaling output, such as IL-2 production, even if the early signaling events measured at 2 min after pMHCII engagement were similar.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Small decreases in responding T1-TP(2C) cells for pCD3ζ and pZAP70 were observed relative to the control.
source: We observed small decreases in responding T1-TP(2C) cells for pCD3ζ and pZAP70 relative to the control, while pPLCγ1 trended lower for this mutant.
evidence: This reports experimental findings.

claim: Mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together in the absence of the intracellular domain can reduce the number of cells that initiate pMHCII-specific signaling.
source: These data indicate that mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together in the absence of the intracellular domain can reduce the number of cells that initiate pMHCII-specific signaling (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplements 1C and 2C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The phenotype of reduced percent responders was not observed in prior study when the intracellular domain was present.
source: We did not observe this phenotype in our prior study when the intracellular domain was present, suggesting this is unique to the absence of the intracellular domain (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This compares current findings to prior work.

claim: For all T1-Palm(3C) and T1-TP(3C) lines, pCD3ζ, pZAP70, and pPLCγ1 levels were significantly lower than the controls.
source: We also measured early signaling for three independently generated T1-Palm(3C) and T1-TP(3C) mutant cell lines compared to their paired T1 controls. For all lines, pCD3ζ, pZAP70, and pPLCγ1 levels were significantly lower than the controls, which was reflected in the normalized fold change (Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B, 2A and B).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The fold change for the T1-TP(3C) levels relative to the T1 was similar to T1-TP(2C).
source: The fold change for the T1-TP(3C) levels relative to the T1 was similar to T1-TP(2C) (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplements 1B and 2B and Table 3).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures and table.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together are key determinants of the LCK-independent contributions that CD4 makes to amplifying pMHCII-specific proximal signaling.
source: These data provide further evidence that the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together are key determinants of the LCK-independent contributions that CD4 makes to amplifying pMHCII-specific proximal signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The percent responders were lower for pCD3ζ and pZAP70 for T1-TP(3C) compared to WT.
source: Finally, the percent responders were lower for pCD3ζ and pZAP70 for T1-TP(3C) compared to WT (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplements 1C and 2C).
evidence: This reports experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: In the absence of the intracellular domain, mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs influences initiation of key signaling events.
source: These data are consistent with the idea that, in the absence of the intracellular domain, mutating these motifs influences initiation of key signaling events.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Computational reconstruction of CD4 evolution provided access to results from experiments that Nature performed over ~435 million years in a greater variety of jawed vertebrates than could be achieved with mouse or human samples in the lab.
source: Our computational reconstruction of CD4 evolution provided access to a subset of results from experiments that Nature performed over ~435 million years in a greater variety of jawed vertebrates, in the wild, than could be achieved with mouse or human samples in the lab (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the evolutionary approach with citation.

claim: Evolutionary analysis allowed identification of residues selected under purifying selection that are predicted to be functionally significant.
source: It allowed us to identify residues that were selected under purifying selection, and are thus predicted to be functionally significant, because acquiring a mutation at these residues would affect fitness and results in a failure to propagate the change to future progeny.
evidence: This describes the rationale for the evolutionary approach.

claim: The data are not consistent with predictions of the prevailing model in which CD4 recruits LCK to CD3 ITAMs to initiate signaling.
source: The data presented here are not consistent with predictions of the prevailing model in which CD4 recruits LCK to CD3 ITAMs to initiate signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Reducing CD4-LCK interactions reduces pMHCII-specific IL-2 production, but this cannot be attributed to reductions in pCD3ζ levels.
source: Importantly, this study builds upon our prior work by showing that while reducing CD4-LCK interactions reduces pMHCII-specific IL-2 production in our system, either by mutating the CQC clasp or removing the CD4 intracellular domain entirely, this cannot be attributed to reductions in pCD3ζ levels as predicted by the TCR signaling paradigm (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings with citation to prior work.

claim: There is a threshold for the number of phosphorylated CD3ζ molecules and/or the duration of signaling that is required to drive IL-2 production in the experimental system.
source: We take these data together as evidence that there is a threshold for the number of phosphorylated CD3ζ molecules, and/or the duration of signaling, that is required to drive IL-2 production in our system.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: CD4 binding to pMHCII functions to increase the number of TCR-CD3 complexes per cell that experience CD3ζ phosphorylation to reach the threshold for IL-2 production and/or sustain signaling.
source: We also conclude that CD4 binding to pMHCII functions to increase the number of TCR-CD3 complexes per cell that experience CD3ζ phosphorylation to reach that threshold and/or sustain signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: There is a density of agonist pMHCII below which CD4 binding to pMHCII is essential for signal initiation.
source: A logical extension of these conclusions is that there is a density of agonist pMHCII below which CD4 binding to pMHCII is essential for signal initiation.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the experimental findings.

claim: CD4 is necessary for signal propagation and amplification to the calcium mobilization step in response to fewer than 25 agonist pMHCII.
source: This idea is supported by findings that CD4 is necessary for signal propagation and amplification to the calcium mobilization step in response to fewer than 25 agonist pMHCII (Irvine et al., 2002).
evidence: This cites prior findings that support the interpretation.

claim: IL-2 production increased significantly when the full intracellular helix was mutated.
source: Furthermore, we found in our prior study that IL-2 production increased significantly when we mutated the full intracellular helix, the helix and CQC clasp together, or the IKRLL motif alone.
evidence: This reports findings from prior work.

claim: IL-2 production increased significantly when the helix and CQC clasp were mutated together.
source: Furthermore, we found in our prior study that IL-2 production increased significantly when we mutated the full intracellular helix, the helix and CQC clasp together, or the IKRLL motif alone.
evidence: This reports findings from prior work.

claim: IL-2 production increased significantly when the IKRLL motif alone was mutated.
source: Furthermore, we found in our prior study that IL-2 production increased significantly when we mutated the full intracellular helix, the helix and CQC clasp together, or the IKRLL motif alone.
evidence: This reports findings from prior work.

claim: The contributions of CD4 to signal initiation and amplification at early timepoints are independent of direct CD4-LCK interactions.
source: These direct tests of the TCR signaling paradigm are inconsistent with predictions of the model. As such, they suggest that the contributions of CD4 to signal initiation and amplification at the early timepoint we measured are independent of direct CD4-LCK interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The combined impact of mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs reduced pCD3ζ levels to ~16% of the contribution of CD4-pMHCII engagement.
source: Because the combined impact of mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs reduced pCD3ζ levels to ~16% of the contribution of CD4-pMHCII engagement, even when direct CD4-LCK interactions were absent, we can conclude that the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are key determinants that help CD4 drive signaling above the threshold required for IL-2 production.
evidence: This reports quantitative findings and interpretation.

claim: Mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together can reduce the frequency of cells experiencing CD3ζ and ZAP70 phosphorylation in the absence of the intracellular domain.
source: Our data also provide evidence that mutating the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together can reduce the frequency of cells experiencing CD3ζ and ZAP70 phosphorylation in the absence of the intracellular domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The switch-like function of the palmitoylation motif may influence signal initiation.
source: Given that palmitoylation is rapidly reversible, these data suggest that the switch-like function of the palmitoylation motif may influence signal initiation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the known reversibility of palmitoylation.

claim: Binding of CD4 and TCR-CD3 to pMHCII can amplify pMHCII-specific signaling without the contributions of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs at high ligand densities, albeit at lower levels.
source: Binding of CD4 and TCR-CD3 to pMHCII can therefore amplify pMHCII-specific signaling without the contributions of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs, or motifs in the intracellular domain, albeit at lower levels than if these motifs are intact.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: There is an agonist pMHCII density below which the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs are essential for the initiation of early signaling events.
source: Given that these motifs were essential for IL-2 production at low ligand densities, a logical extension of these data is that there is an agonist pMHCII density below which these motifs are essential for the initiation of early signaling events.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the experimental findings.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs do not influence early signaling events by regulating the ability of CD4 to recruit LCK to or sequester it away from the TCR-CD3 ITAMs.
source: The data from our current study indicate that the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs do not influence early signaling events by regulating the ability of CD4 to either recruit LCK to, or sequester it away from, the TCR-CD3 ITAMs as we previously postulated (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings that revises a prior hypothesis.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs work independently of CD4-LCK interactions to enhance pMHCII-specific signaling.
source: Instead, they work independently of CD4-LCK interactions to enhance pMHCII-specific signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Palmitate moieties can sandwich cholesterol against the flat surface of a GG patch on a transmembrane domain helix in other proteins.
source: It is tempting to speculate that because these motifs can regulate CD4 membrane domain localization and, because in other proteins palmitate moieties can sandwich cholesterol against the flat surface of a GG patch on a transmembrane domain helix, these motifs may allow CD4 to regulate local concentration of cholesterol or cholesterol sulfate around TCR-CD3, perhaps by taking such molecules away from TCR-CD3 to stabilize allosteric changes associated with signaling (Chen et al., 2022; Fessler, 2016; Gil et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2015; Song et al., 2014; Swamy et al., 2016; Teese and Langosch, 2015; Wacker et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited knowledge about other proteins.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs may allow CD4 to regulate local concentration of cholesterol or cholesterol sulfate around TCR-CD3.
source: It is tempting to speculate that because these motifs can regulate CD4 membrane domain localization and, because in other proteins palmitate moieties can sandwich cholesterol against the flat surface of a GG patch on a transmembrane domain helix, these motifs may allow CD4 to regulate local concentration of cholesterol or cholesterol sulfate around TCR-CD3, perhaps by taking such molecules away from TCR-CD3 to stabilize allosteric changes associated with signaling (Chen et al., 2022; Fessler, 2016; Gil et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2015; Song et al., 2014; Swamy et al., 2016; Teese and Langosch, 2015; Wacker et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited knowledge.

claim: CD4 motifs may impact the accessibility of ITAMs for LCK phosphorylation by changing the local membrane environment around TCR-CD3 upon reciprocal engagement of pMHCII.
source: These CD4 motifs may also impact the accessibility of ITAMs for LCK phosphorylation by changing the local membrane environment around TCR-CD3 upon reciprocal engagement of pMHCII (Aivazian and Stern, 2000; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited knowledge.

claim: G402 of the GGXXG motif has covaried over evolutionary time with L438 of the intracellular helix IKRLL motif.
source: Finally, it is worth considering that, in our prior study, we found G402 of the GGXXG motif has covaried over evolutionary time with L438 of the intracellular helix IKRLL motif that has inhibitory function, suggesting that the function of these motifs are co-evolving (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This reports findings from prior work.

claim: The function of the GGXXG and IKRLL motifs are co-evolving.
source: Finally, it is worth considering that, in our prior study, we found G402 of the GGXXG motif has covaried over evolutionary time with L438 of the intracellular helix IKRLL motif that has inhibitory function, suggesting that the function of these motifs are co-evolving (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an interpretation of evolutionary analysis from prior work.

claim: The signal enhancing activity of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together counterbalanced the inhibitory activity of the IKRLL motif with regard to IL-2 production.
source: In support of this idea, we reported that the signal enhancing activity of the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs together counterbalanced the inhibitory activity of the IKRLL motif with regard to IL-2 production.
evidence: This reports findings from prior work.

claim: pMHCII-specific signaling is not initiated or dependent on CD4 recruitment of LCK kinase activity to the CD3 ITAMs.
source: Altogether, the data in this and our preceding study provide direct evidence that complement indirect results indicating that pMHCII-specific signaling is not initiated, or dependent on, CD4 recruitment of LCK kinase activity to the CD3 ITAMs (Glassman et al., 2018; Horkova et al., 2023; Killeen and Littman, 1993; Lee et al., 2022; Xu and Littman, 1993).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings with citation to supporting work.

claim: Recent work on CD8 suggests that this coreceptor also does not recruit LCK to phosphorylate CD3 ITAMs.
source: Recent work on CD8 suggest that this coreceptor also does not recruit LCK to phosphorylate CD3 ITAMs (Casas et al., 2014; Wei et al., 2020).
evidence: This cites recent findings about CD8.

claim: The TCR signaling paradigm needs revising as it pertains to coreceptor-LCK interactions.
source: In total, these findings suggest that the TCR signaling paradigm needs revising as it pertains to coreceptor-LCK interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the cumulative evidence.

claim: For CD4, reciprocal binding of CD4 and TCR-CD3 enables free LCK and FYN to initiate signaling by phosphorylating the ITAMs and ZAP70.
source: For CD4, the existing evidence suggest that reciprocal binding of CD4 and TCR-CD3 enables free LCK and FYN to initiate signaling by phosphorylating the ITAMs and ZAP70 (Glassman et al., 2016; Glassman et al., 2018; Horkova et al., 2023; Lee et al., 2022; Salmond et al., 2009; van Oers et al., 1996).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on cited evidence.

claim: The GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs work together to enhance early signaling events independently of direct CD4-LCK interactions.
source: The contribution of the current study is in showing the GGXXG and (C/F)CV+C motifs work together to enhance these early signaling events independently of direct CD4-LCK interactions.
evidence: This summarizes the main contribution of the current study.

claim: Data from two studies suggest that LCK makes a kinase-independent contribution to pMHCII-specific responses.
source: Data from two studies suggest that LCK makes a kinase-independent contribution to pMHCII-specific responses; it is therefore plausible that the phenotype reported for CD4 when the CQC clasp is mutated is due to relieving the kinase-independent scaffolding function of LCK (Horkova et al., 2023; Xu and Littman, 1993).
evidence: This cites studies suggesting a kinase-independent role for LCK.

claim: The phenotype reported for CD4 when the CQC clasp is mutated may be due to relieving the kinase-independent scaffolding function of LCK.
source: Data from two studies suggest that LCK makes a kinase-independent contribution to pMHCII-specific responses; it is therefore plausible that the phenotype reported for CD4 when the CQC clasp is mutated is due to relieving the kinase-independent scaffolding function of LCK (Horkova et al., 2023; Xu and Littman, 1993).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited evidence.

claim: Mutating the CQC clasp would favor helix interactions with other putative partners.
source: In addition, CD4-LCK interaction via the CQC clasp motif and the intracellular helix will prevent the helix from interacting with other partners, thus mutating the CQC clasp would favor helix interactions with other putative partners (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited prior work.

claim: The CQC clasp is thought to play a role in positioning CD4 in proximity to LAT.
source: Finally, the CQC clasp is thought to play a role in positioning CD4 in proximity to LAT, either through direct or indirect interactions, which could contribute to the phenotype of CQC clasp mutants (Bosselut et al., 1999; Lo et al., 2018; Lo et al., 2019).
evidence: This cites prior work suggesting a role for the CQC clasp in CD4-LAT positioning.

claim: If CD4-LCK and CD4-LAT interactions are mutually exclusive and both require the CQC clasp, then mutating this motif would have a greater impact than just relieving CD4-LCK interactions.
source: If CD4-LCK and CD4-LAT interactions are mutually exclusive, and both require the CQC clasp, then mutating this motif would have a greater impact than just relieving CD4-LCK interactions (Bosselut et al., 1999).
evidence: This is speculation based on cited knowledge.

claim: The biochemical and biophysical bases for interactions between CD4 and its interacting partners should be the same in 58α-β- cells as in thymocytes or in different CD4+ T cells.
source: Our approach allows us to identify functionally important residues/motif and then interrogate basic mechanistic principles of their function that should hold true across CD4+ T cell subsets since the biochemical and biophysical bases for interactions between CD4 and its interacting partners (i.e. other proteins or membrane components) should be the same in 58α-β- cells as in thymocytes or in different CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the findings.

claim: Different CD4+ T cell populations will have different levels of expression of relevant proteins.
source: However, different CD4+ T cell populations will have different levels of expression of relevant proteins (e.g. interacting partners or modifying enzymes), and may even have differences in lipid composition, such that the impact of the motifs we have identified and studied to date may lead to different outcomes in different CD4+ T cell subsets (http://immpres.co.uk/) (Tuosto and Xu, 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about biological variability with citation.

claim: Differences in expression of enzymes with switch-like functions may vary between naïve CD4+ T cells, different Th subsets, or Tregs to differentially tune the activity of CD4 motifs.
source: For example, differences in expression of enzymes with switch-like functions, such as those that add or remove palmitate to the (C/F)CV+C motif, or those that phosphorylate or dephosphorylate the serines in the intracellular helix that regulate CD4-LCK interactions and inhibitory activity, may vary between naïve CD4+ T cells, different Th subsets, or Tregs to differentially tune the activity of these motifs and their impact on pMHCII-specific signaling.
evidence: This is speculation about how the motifs might function differently in different cell types.

claim: 58α-β- T cell hybridoma lines were generated from parental 58α-β- T cell hybridoma cells by retroviral transduction.
source: 58α-β- T cell hybridoma lines were generated from Kuhns Lab stocks of parental 58α-β- T cell hybridoma cells (obtained from YH Chien at Stanford University) by retroviral transduction and maintained in culture by standard techniques as previously described (Glassman et al., 2018; Letourneur and Malissen, 1989).
evidence: This describes the methods used with citations.

claim: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas lack expression of endogenous TCRα and TCRβ chains.
source: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas lack expression of endogenous TCRα and TCRβ chains, are CD4 negative, make IL-2 in response to TCR signaling, and are variant of the DO-11.10.7 mouse T cell hybridoma (Balb/c T cell fused to BW5147 thymoma) (Letourneur and Malissen, 1989).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the cell line with citation.

claim: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas are CD4 negative.
source: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas lack expression of endogenous TCRα and TCRβ chains, are CD4 negative, make IL-2 in response to TCR signaling, and are variant of the DO-11.10.7 mouse T cell hybridoma (Balb/c T cell fused to BW5147 thymoma) (Letourneur and Malissen, 1989).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the cell line with citation.

claim: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas make IL-2 in response to TCR signaling.
source: 58α-β- T cell hybridomas lack expression of endogenous TCRα and TCRβ chains, are CD4 negative, make IL-2 in response to TCR signaling, and are variant of the DO-11.10.7 mouse T cell hybridoma (Balb/c T cell fused to BW5147 thymoma) (Letourneur and Malissen, 1989).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the cell line with citation.
